_comment: Human pressure-relief valve applied by build_classmap.py AFTER RxClass + legacy tags. Order: (1) start from legacy_drugclasses tags ∪ RxClass-derived tags; (2) union pin_classes; (3) remove deny_classes; (4) drop exclude_generics; (5) register alias_generics into the brands/generics maps. Pins guarantee the clinically critical classifications even when an open source under-classifies; denies preserve deliberate legacy scoping.
_notes_august_2026_ddi_fixes: Ported 2026-10-02 from the August R1-reviewed fixes that were hand-edited into interaction-rules.js only (qa-report/clinical_safety.md; commits 34fc51533 CR1-CR3, 4f3180121, b2a23bcaa + 3f9550bf0 HIGH, b2889f7f9 + 0905c1a58 MEDIUM). Pins: cyp2c9_inhibitor (CR1, warfarin), cotrimoxazole = co-trimoxazole (CR1 hyphen bug), paracetamol analgesic (CR3), cyp1a2_inhibitor (M follow-up, theophylline), bare insulin (M5, insulin + sulfonylurea), systemic_corticosteroid (M follow-up: steroid + NSAID fires for systemic steroids only). Denies: verapamil is not a DHP (M3; mech-cyp3a4strong-nondhp-ccb covers clarithromycin), lisinopril is not a thiazide (H4), clozapine is not a benzodiazepine (M3), protamine/citrate/edetate are not anticoagulants and fondaparinux/bivalirudin not DOACs (H follow-up), abciximab/zonisamide/sarecycline are not P-gp inhibitors (H follow-up). Rules: mechanism_rules.json (20); superseded legacy rules retired in legacy_rules.json.
_notes_2026_10_02: Owner-approved. build_gold.py no longer reads 'Non-opioid' as opioid (nor non-benzodiazepine, non-NSAID, Non-dihydropyridine, insulin secretagogue/sensitizer). Pins: nefopam, flupirtine, noscapine, levocloperastine keep cns_depressant (central and sedating, but NOT opioids). verapamil's dihydropyridine_ccb pin was removed the same day: mech-cyp3a4strong-nondhp-ccb now ships in both artifacts (see _notes_august_2026_ddi_fixes). buspirone: not a benzodiazepine or CNS depressant, but serotonergic (serotonin syndrome with tramadol, SSRIs/SNRIs; labelled against MAOIs and linezolid), pinned so removing its wrong tags does not leave it with no alert (R1, owner 2026-10-02). Deny: naloxone is an antagonist, not an opioid or CNS depressant. naltrexone is deliberately left tagged opioid + cns_depressant until an opioid antagonist + agonist rule is signed off (its wrong tag is today the only alert for naltrexone + morphine).
